text: Become independent. Follow the teachings. Come for satsangs. Read the books, all the literature available in the spiritual field. Do your meditation regularly and carry on.
author: Sri M

text: One-pointedness is a complete stillness of mind where there is no thought whatsoever.
author: Sri M

text: To be eternally vigilant is the beginning of the journey. The amount of effort you put into it has its own reward. When the mind, after a while, becomes so sensitive that nothing can escape it, then you don’t have to deliberately do it.
author: Sri M

text: We cannot do anything about the past so we have to work with the present, something now. It’s simple like the breeze that is blowing in here. We are generally not even aware of the breeze.
author: Sri M

text: It’s quite natural that sometimes the mind would want an excuse, give it a little leeway and then say come on enough, come back, pull it. nothing should be carried to fanatic limits, follow the middle path. In the beginning if you keep tightening the noose, the mind may rebel and you may not be able to control it.
author: Sri M

text: If you want to delve deep into the layers of your consciousness and finally reach the essence, then meditation is a must.
author: Sri M

text: When a person has unquestioned faith in his own capacity for achieving a goal, whether spiritual or temporal, he/she is not disturbed by negative thoughts that weaken the will and discourage the spirit. He persists in his efforts till the very end and attains what he sets out to do.
author: Sri M

text: Change has to come from within, it cannot be brought from outside.
author: Sri M

text: The ancient teachers said that there is a link between your breathing pattern and your emotional states, and if you change the rhythm or pattern of your breath, you can change your emotional state. You can change your mood.
author: Sri M

text: If you say that I depend on God or the Supreme Being and ask for help to fend yourself from the disasters that happen to you and not give up, that is the best way to move forward. Surrender and hard work both have to go together especially in spiritual life.
author: Sri M

text: The world is a testing point. Therefore we need some periods of solitude to figure out that we have a deep sea of peace and happiness within.
author: Sri M

text: If you think that by gathering knowledge one becomes a great wise person, you are absolutely wrong. All knowledge is memory, something in the past. If you are looking for Truth, it is always present, not something in the past. So what we have is not the Truth but the idea of the truth stored as a memory.
author: Sri M

text: When you are in natural settings, not man-made, it's easier for the mind to be meditative. So, the closer you are with things that are not man made, the mind expands and gets into a meditative state.
author: Sri M

text: If you have a slate, every time you write on it, you have to rub it off to write anything else: otherwise, if you overwrite, you can neither read it, nor is there any space to do more writing. So, in matters of inner exploration, the most important thing is to keep your slate clean.
author: Sri M

text: Consciousness is a living entity and your emotions, thought processes, everything is reflected from it. It is the core of your emotions, it is the awareness from which everything starts.
author: Sri M

text: When all the movement of the mind, which is all the time moving and reaching out, ends, then what is left? The seeker and his true essence, which is without any effort. Then the seeker is the sought. There is no difference.
author: Sri M

text: Mukti is a state of mind which comes when we begin to understand that we cannot free ourselves temporarily. When we begin to understand that all the influences in the world, major influence being our own mind, is binding us and not allowing us to be free, is the beginning of understanding what mukti is. First to understand that I am not mukta. We go around thinking that we are actually free.
author: Sri M

text: The Vedantic understanding is that the only reality - absolute reality and not relative reality, is the witness.
author: Sri M

text: We are always trying to become complete and better, but we never do because if we did, we wouldn't try anymore. I am not saying you shouldn't try, just realise that this Poornata comes when the mind is not becoming but is at rest. Now in the midst of the becoming is it possible to be at rest? We are saying yes. That process is called Sadhana and when That is touched, then one is free.
author: Sri M

text: If you want to do something which you really love to do, you have to find time.
author: Sri M

text: Desire is the root of all sorrow. Nirvana is freedom from sorrow for all mankind. This means unless one is free of desire, one cannot have Nirvana, which is the Buddhist terminology for mukti.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is the removal of all the distractions and the opposite thoughts and tensions of the mind.
author: Sri M

text: For the mind to attain peace, you don't have to go anywhere. Short periods of solitude are very good. Then when you come back you carry a little bit of peace back to your work and gradually you become stabilised in that inner peace. When you are stabilised, then you are moving towards freedom.
author: Sri M

text: The Bhagavad Gita comes from the Bhishma Parva of the Mahabharata. It expresses the truths of the Upanishads and the Brahma Sutra in practical, simple, direct terms for us to understand. This is the importance of the Bhagavad Gita.
author: Sri M

text: Sit quietly and look within. Thoughts of course will come and go. Don't bother. Sit. Any thought that comes, cut it with your own thought.
author: Sri M

text: If we figure out that freedom, Mukti that we seek is nowhere to be searched but deep within us, when this is found, then we are free.
author: Sri M

text: The happiness that you seek is inside each one of us. If we can focus on that, then we have found the way to Mukti, freedom. Is it easy? It is not difficult. Is it difficult? No, it is easy. Why? Because it is a change of attitude basically.
author: Sri M

text: Gita is not something to be read as a theoretical text. While you need to do that, it basically should be looked at as a sadhana, a practice by which you free yourself.
author: Sri M

text: If you choose the spiritual path you should understand that it is not an easy path and therefore you need to put all your attention on it. If you take it as a hobby, it won't work. Therefore make it your primary purpose and don't give up. You will often fall down but you need to get up and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: Knowing begins with not knowing. If you know already, then you cannot learn. Everybody is quick to say, I know. The fact is, when you say you know, then you are not learning anymore. Your mind has blocked itself.
author: Sri M

text: In the Dream state, when you understand it for what it actually is, that it's an entire illusion built up from the beginning of creation and the origin is you, not what has originated then you recede from all these illusions and go into reality.
author: Sri M

text: The ultimate cannot be measured and from my understanding consciousness is the original feature of this entire web that has been built around pure consciousness for its own reason. We do not know why it bubbles out into this illusion and then goes back again into pure consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: Recognize divinity in all living beings, especially in human beings. And therefore, forgive their shortcomings. That's the best way to live.
author: Sri M

text: Kumbha is a pot and Purna Kumbha means full pot. Kumbha is actually a description of what we call in yoga as Kumbhak meaning when your belly is filled with air. From our point of view Purna Kumbha is when the belly is completely filled with air and if you are a real Kriya Yogi you do not have the need to exhale. But don't try that out, you might damage your lungs!
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher need not necessarily be someone who lives in the Himalayas for hundreds of years. He may be living in your back house!. There are hundreds of people living in the Himalayas. Are they all great spiritual teachers? For that, you need experience. You have to walk; you have to move; you have to find out for yourself.
author: Sri M

text: The sadhak has to be very careful. The Upanishads have described the spiritual path as shurasya dhaara , it is like walking on the ‘edge of a razor’. It is dangerous and difficult. Walking on the edge of a razor, you can get cut or fall this side or that. Therefore it is quite a serious affair. It is not entertainment.
author: Sri M

text: We all know we are the body. Slowly, we start thinking and we begin to realise that I cannot be the body because the body belongs to me and what belongs to me cannot be me. This is not me. Then what am I? Who am I? When one thinks like this, then one proceeds looking into this question carefully and one pursues it.
author: Sri M

text: It is by itself a contradiction for the limited to seek the unlimited. When the limited understands its limitations and then says this is not the way to find it, it becomes quiet. It is only then, there is hope that the other will make itself known.
author: Sri M

text: Sit down and meditate in your heart center and whenever thoughts which are not related to the inner come, try to keep them away.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t run away from sorrows and the problems of the world because wherever you go, you carry your mind with you. Stay where you are and deal with the situation.
author: Sri M

text: Whether you are an intellectual or what normally can be called a non-intellectual, irrespective of this, the most important condition to find the Truth is an intense desire.
author: Sri M

text: As your feelings become more and more subtle, deeper centers of the human mind open up to form a link to that which is beyond the ordinary mind.
author: Sri M

text: Be a bhakta more than anything else because through bhakti all jnana will dawn.
author: Sri M

text: Amrita comes from the word ‘ a – mrita’ which means immortal or deathless. It does not mean physical deathlessness. All the great sages have come and gone. Nobody remains forever. It means the realization that there is something in us that is immortal and which survives the body.
author: Sri M

text: This world is beautiful. It is complete in and of itself. There is no harm in giving and sharing love. But the problem starts when it becomes an obsession, when I become possessive about it, when I want it only for myself.
author: Sri M

text: When Kabir Das wove, everyone thought he was weaving cloth. Actually, he was weaving from the warp and weft of love and devotion.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation is any activity that brings about love, affection, the calmness of mind, and tranquility leading to the ultimate goal.
author: Sri M

text: When the love for the Divine arises, it’s like an overflow. There are no questions.
author: Sri M

text: If the mind is made up of thoughts and thoughts are always vibrating, moving - sometimes up, sometimes down, constantly in motion; that movement of thought or the waves of thoughts are known as vrittis . The stopping of the vrittis – that complete stopping of the movement of the vrittis , is considered to be yoga or Yogas Chitta Vritti Nirodha .
author: Sri M

text: If one understands that one is not the body but the inner self which is consciousness, then one begins to understand how to deal with sorrow. But unless and until some kind of sorrow comes, one does not realize the unreality of existence and wake up from it. Sorrow shakes one up.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna, the manifestation of the Supreme Being says that if you would only fix your attention on ‘me’, with complete faith, absolute attention and great love, then I will certainly save you from the ocean of birth and death.
author: Sri M

text: Trishul while it represents the weapon which keeps away all negativity and all negative energy, in the human being as a yogi, it represents the Ida, Pingala, and the Sushumna, which is why the Sushumna is usually longer.
author: Sri M

text: Shiva is dancing on Apasmara, a sign of ego, ignorance and non-intelligent living, which takes one to destruction. If you are leading such a life, if Shiva decides to dance on you and trample you, be happy, it will take you to the realms of happiness and peace, and no happiness and peace happens until one goes through some churning or the other. If you say everything is hunky dory but I still want to find the Truth, you cannot. You are not allowing Shiva to dismantle the structure. If you don't dismantle the structure, you will not find the essence.
author: Sri M

text: In the dance of Tandava Nritya, everything is removed and shattered, and there is only Shivam, pure Shivam. If one is ready for that, then one has become Shiva. Then only you can say chidananda roopah shivoham, don't keep on chanting it without reaching that stage.
author: Sri M

text: Om Namah Shivaya is one of the great Maha Mantras, described in the Agamas, Upanishads, Puranas, Shiva Samhita. Om means the Supreme Being beyond the grasp of the senses. Namah Shivaya means I bow down to that Shiva, that supreme bliss. In Sanskrit, Shivam also means blissfulness, Ananda. Om Namah Shivaya - I bow down to that supreme bliss who is in the form of Shiva.
author: Sri M

text: The coming together, union of Shiva and Parvati is celebrated as Shivaratri. During the dance of Shiva, Tandava Nritya with the Damaru, there is no other sound except the sound of the Damaru. Yogis who meditate and go deep, will first hear the heart beat sounding like a Damaru. Shiva is dancing the dance of destruction, so is it destruction? It is not. It is regeneration. Because if the old is not destroyed, there is no space for the new in this world. If ignorance is not destroyed, there is no place for knowledge in this world. Therefore the Tandava Nritya, where everything shakes, is a demolition, so that new things come.
author: Sri M

text: The highest experience of the yogis is when Shiva is experienced as one's own inner being. chidananda roopah shivoham shivoham - I am of the nature of chit, consciousness and Ananda, bliss. I am Shivam Shivam, I am auspiciousness, I am auspiciousness.
author: Sri M

text: When one goes within and touches That, one realizes that the outer is not different from the inner.
author: Sri M

text: It’s only when the mind settles down that the inner being manifests.
author: Sri M

text: Because our puny little brains cannot understand the plan of life. We think our plan is the best plan. Well, it is not or it may not be.
author: Sri M

text: Supreme Brahman is present everywhere not in any particular place.
author: Sri M

text: When dharana becomes effortless and quiet, it naturally goes into dhyana. In that dhyana state even ‘I’ does not exist.
author: Sri M

text: When we say control your thoughts during meditation, it is impossible to control and make them disappear. Because the moment you try to make thoughts disappear, you are thinking.
author: Sri M

text: The only true Apara-vidya , which leads to Vijnana , is the non-verbal transcendental experience of the Supreme Truth. It takes place when the mind becomes absolutely still, having discovered the uselessness of mental acrobatics. Thus it is free from every trap which the thought lays.
author: Sri M

text: Good and evil, famous and notorious, darkness and light, positive and negative, all are in the Supreme Being and yet in its essential essence the Supreme Godhead is not affected by the opposites.
author: Sri M

text: The Buddhists say, ‘One who has walked across’ - paraa gati – ‘one who has gone beyond’, such a person is called ‘Bodhi’, one who has the ‘bodh’. ‘Gate Gate Pāragate Pārasamgate Bodhi Svāhā ’ - ‘May I also be like that Bodhi’.
author: Sri M

text: If the mind is made up of thoughts and thoughts are always vibrating, constantly in motion; that movement of thought or the waves of thoughts are known as vrittis . The stopping of the vrittis , complete stopping of the movement, is considered to be yoga or Yogas Chitta Vritti Nirodha.
author: Sri M

text: The whole principle of life is - something coming in and something going out. Nobody can stop it, and no amount of anything can help to get out. So to accept it and be, this is the sign of going deeper into your own self.
author: Sri M

text: If one learns to live within oneself, without being dependent on any external factor then one is free.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual journey is not a search for power. It’s a search for peace, happiness and quietude. Because you are spiritually on a higher level, you may have some power, that is different. But if you begin the spiritual search because of power, then you are not searching for spirit.
author: Sri M

text: Jyotisham is a Vedanga. It means astronomy, science of the stars, Jyot - of the lighted objects. Astrology is a small part of Jyotisha.
author: Sri M

text: When the Kurukshketra battle takes place within, you have to face it, you cannot run. While doing it, watch yourself carefully and see what is your motive. Why am I doing this and in that process if some things drop off, let them drop off. Don’t get too concerned about it. Nothing will happen, sky is not going to fall on your head. What if it falls! After all it is the sky, so be free.
author: Sri M

text: All things that have come out of the void, go back into the void.
author: Sri M

text: When is it divine will? There are some good things which divine will can make happen, but since we are not attuned to it, we consider it as — what is this stuff, why is God troubling me so much! It’s the trouble that makes you rise up beyond the fact.
author: Sri M

text: Nature has this very peculiar habit: when you run behind something, it runs away from you. When you say — I’m okay, if it comes, then it comes.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot meditate or be spiritual all twenty-four hours. So, what do you do with the rest of the time? You need to initiate some action which is good for others because then you shed the dross of your own mind by empathising with others and helping them out. Gradually when the mind is purified, you can also meditate properly.
author: Sri M

text: It's not easy to sit down and meditate when your mind is full of crude, selfish, and self-centred emotions. One way to break that is to help the unfortunate.
author: Sri M

text: Everybody has a little bit of tamas, rajas, and s attva, the proportion being different in each person. The main problem is when, especially those on the spiritual path, begin to mistake tamas for sattva. Because sattva is also by nature actionless, quiet, and tranquil. In sattva guna, you don't have to do any activity. Very often, the tamoguna is mistaken for sattva.
author: Sri M

text: What is the way to convert tamoguna into sattva ? Action. Do some work, so that the tamas is converted into rajas and, when rajas (action) is oriented towards the good of others, then it takes you into sattva and from sattva , you finally reach the state which is beyond all gunas. You can't jump from tamoguna to that which is beyond all gunas. It’s a gradual process.
author: Sri M

text: We all want to be happy in some way. The only permanent ananda available to us is that which is real is within, as opposed to that which is here today and gone tomorrow.
author: Sri M

text: While I advocate that you try to remain with a happy attitude of mind, don't neglect the fact that this cannot be sustained until we find the inner happiness which is in us. When that is found, then you can sustain it. Till then, if it falls, try to recover and come back. That's all you can do on this earth.
author: Sri M

text: Everybody is swimming along the stream. The moment you start a spiritual practice, the moment you turn in another direction, swim against the stream, it becomes a tussle. There is no way out except to fight it out. There is no shortcut. Keep reiterating that this is the most important thing you have to do.
author: Sri M

text: On the spiritual path, it's not so easy to fit in but then you can't totally break free from the world. You stay with it until you become really mature in your spiritual field. Then you have to do nothing. What is not necessary will fall off. And what is required will remain.
author: Sri M

text: It's the nature of the world that it protects you as long as you are not mature, like a baby in the womb. And once you are mature, the same muscles push you out. So, don't worry. Thank the world for providing you with food, for shelter etc. Continue with your practices till it becomes not so difficult to adjust between the two worlds.
author: Sri M

text: No new thing has been found without somebody asking — is this possible? Even scientific discoveries have happened because some people were sceptical about what they thought was real and said — no, we need to explore.
author: Sri M

text: The science of yoga is that which can deliberately change your brain’s chemical composition. Once it has changed, you can probably explore and go beyond it. It's to free yourself from the limitations of the conditioned brain.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is absolutely quiet and tranquil, it becomes the tarmac from which you can take off to regions which are outside of our ordinary brain.
author: Sri M

text: How can our brain be absolutely quiet? Only when there are no distractions whatsoever, no contradictions pulling on either side. When the brain is absolutely calm, then there is something which is outside, which is beyond. This, one can only know through experience, and for experience, we need to follow procedure. Although the procedure ultimately takes you out of all procedures!
author: Sri M

text: The Divine can never sleep. In the Quran, there is a beautiful verse – ‘He’ is called ‘the Sleepless One’ because if he falls asleep, the whole world will collapse.
author: Sri M

text: Naama Smarana is one of the easiest and the best. Along with that you should also take care of other aspects of life, little disciplines that one should follow. The most important root discipline from which other things come is less for the self and more for the others. This is the way to the spiritual field.
author: Sri M

text: Can our ‘sundown’ be the name of God? Can we listen to that music which moves our hearts and opens the doors to extra sensory perceptions? I am not talking about powers. There are centers in the human system, other than the ones used by the ordinary human mind to solve its day to day material problems.
author: Sri M

text: Bhajans, kirtan , going to places where people worship and going on pilgrimages lead you to the stimulation of the emotional parts of your minds, for opening up centers that you can experience.
author: Sri M

text: The root of sorrow is the wrong identity. One thinks one is the body. And being body oriented, one gets all the sorrows. One experiences sorrows because anything that happens to the body and anything in relationship with other bodies – is the cause of sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: Be a bhakta more than anything else because through bhakti all jnana will dawn.
author: Sri M

text: Most of the activities of the world that we perform, based on the assumption that we are the body, bind us down to the earth. Karma Yoga is the theory or teaching which says, that if you can act knowing well that you are actually the supreme ever free self and not the body, then none of these activities can bind you down to sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: Dependence of the Guru alone could be an obstacle and one has to be very careful about. A genuine teacher never wants you to be dependent on him.
author: Sri M

text: Perhaps the only way to get the mind free from the trappings of the material world is to live in the midst of it, get guidance from the teacher, and come to terms with the world so that one may transcend it at the proper time.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual journey starts when you have experienced life and decided that apart from day-to-day existence, there must be something more . It can’t be just this - in which we are born, get married or unmarried, have kids, have a business or a job, then in the end, die. Is this all to life or there could be something else?
author: Sri M

text: Intelligence has to realize when its function is over and allow something else to take over. That instrument of perception that takes over is known as intuition, Jnana Drishti . You will see Shiva meditating with eyes closed and one small eye in the centre of the forehead. That eye is the eye of perception of the highest and goes beyond the function of the ordinary brain.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes what we think are woes, sorrow, pain or a loss may be a great gain from the spiritual point of view.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t unnecessarily complicate life with too many things. Speak the truth; More than speaking the truth, think the truth. That does not mean that when you speak the truth you have to be blunt. There are sweet ways of speaking the truth. You need not be brusque and then suffer because of that.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher sometimes provides opportunities and situations, either deliberately or as they happen. He does not encourage people to run away from situations but to pause and remain. It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances, one begins to realise for oneself where one stands.
author: Sri M

text: Those who choose to be happy, whatever be the circumstances, will try and be happy. This is not always possible because we are faced with so many challenges and sometimes we get caught up in the cobweb of pain alternating with pleasure. The permanent solution is to go deep within and find that there is a great deal of happiness which is not affected by any outward happening. It's a fountainhead of all happiness inside, which is why it is called Satchidananda .
author: Sri M

text: Bhagavad Gita comes from the Bhishma Parva of the Mahabharata, and it kind of expresses the truths of the Upanishads and the Brahma Sutra in practical, simple, direct terms for you and me to understand.
author: Sri M

text: In very simple words, the meaning of the Gita is found by reversing the word Gita - tagi. Thakur Sri Ramakrishna said, instead of Gita, if you say tagi (Tyagi) , that is the essence of the Gita. The key point is tyaga, letting go, because without that the essence of the Gita is not understood.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga simply means the effort and the approach and the path to find the Truth. So sadhana is required.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Letting go’ means not being stuck to the dream world that we have created for ourselves, and to be able to let go of it at any instant is not easy. It's a long journey and we go through many obstacles and difficulties.
author: Sri M

text: Any approach to the spiritual usually starts when one goes through pain, obstacles to our advancement, when we want something, we don't get it. Then we begin to think, is life just this much or is there something more?
author: Sri M

text: Gita is not something to be read as a theoretical text. While you need to do that, it should be looked at as a sadhana, a practice by which you free yourself.
author: Sri M

text: In para bhakti, all that the devotee asks for is the darshan of the Lord. Even separation sometimes is enjoyed.
author: Sri M

text: The wisest man very soon discovers the limitations of the intellect. The Upanishads declare, yanmanasā na manute yenāhurmano matam , that which even the mind cannot understand, that is the Supreme Reality.
author: Sri M

text: Bhakti cannot be cultivated. It either happens, or it does not happen. It’s only with grace, we cannot say anything. We can do puja etc and, all that is fine. When the heart becomes tender, it happens
author: Sri M

text: Knowing oneself starts with knowing oneself in the midst of people, not alone. In seclusion, I don’t see how I am. We should first know who we are and where we stand. To know thyself means knowing myself as I am, instead of just repeating ‘I am the Brahman’! I can’t be angry, jealous, narrow and still be Brahman.
author: Sri M

text: All our thought processes are made up of language. Music is something which cuts across all barriers.
author: Sri M

text: It doesn’t matter what your belief is. If you need to survive in this world, you need to put in hard work.
author: Sri M

text: The actual aim of understanding the Gita is to go beyond all construction, words, and all conditioning until the Supreme Brahman is face to face with you.
author: Sri M

text: Like the frog that lives on Earth and water, the one who has understood the Truth, whose mind is anchored to the Spirit, can live in this world also.
author: Sri M

text: Most of the activities of the world that we perform, based on the assumption that we are the body, bind us down to the Earth. Karma Yoga is the theory or teaching which says, that if you can act knowing well that you are actually the supreme ever free self and not the body, then none of these activities can bind you down to sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: Sanyasa is not for the lazy. A true sanyasin is one who lives in this world, and acts without worrying too much about the results of the action.
author: Sri M

text: If you work and surrender the fruits of your actions to the Lord, then, such a person is working, but doing detached work. Such a person quickly moves towards the path of meditation because the mind becomes quiet. It is not work that is disturbing your mind, it’s the expectation that is disturbing your mind.
author: Sri M

text: The essence of spiritual practice is that you understand and face that you yourself can use your mind to degrade your mind or raise it up. So, what is the greatest raising up of the mind? When, at least theoretically, you understand that you are not different from the Supreme Brahman, a spark of that reality is in us.
author: Sri M

text: Most of our life is dependent on public opinion. Is it possible to say that, no matter what anybody says, good or bad, I am actually an essence of the Supreme being which is poorna or full by itself?
author: Sri M

text: If you have a healthy body, you have a healthy mind. If you have a healthy mind then you understand the inner realities. So, therefore, start with yoga which gives you a healthy body.
author: Sri M

text: Disconnected is what we imagine. Not being disconnected is what is the Reality. When you find that which you seek in the outside world, when you find it inside. Then you realize that there has been no disconnect. That disconnect was also part of your thinking.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is always seeking fulfillment and it has not learned that the fulfillment is inside. So, while it’s still there, keep trying until you can taste a little bit. Once the taste gets into you, then you’ll start seeing that the gap almost disappears little by little.
author: Sri M

text: We make ourselves limited by thinking that we are limited. Why don’t we for once, at least in our mind, let go of this limitedness!. In this wide world, I am just like a speck of sand. Am I so important, or is the world important?
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishads say that the Truth is something which is far and yet so near; it moves but it’s faster than any movement. It’s that which is, and not that which was. Every minute, it is new.
author: Sri M

text: Ultimately, you are your own Master. There is no other. A teacher can help you understand this point. If you do, then you are free. My job is to tell you that your teacher is in you.
author: Sri M

text: The Truth that we seek is almost like no-thing. Which is why the Buddha called it Shunya. When ego becomes zero, then I see that zero. That Nothing is the essence of everything.
author: Sri M

text: We have forgotten to sit under trees. In ancient times, all the teachers sat under the tree and taught. The Buddha got his enlightenment under a peepal tree.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Buddha, desire is the root of all sorrow and freedom from desire is freedom from sorrow for all mankind.
author: Sri M

text: It’s more important to understand the teachings than to worship the teacher. The sacred is always around us and in our hearts.
author: Sri M

text: When Buddha said to his monks - ‘Go Forth!’, he didn’t mean to only walk, he also meantgetting out of the stagnant little pool that we have created. Move!
author: Sri M

text: Sleep is like a mini-death. So, can we get up in the morning fresh and see as if everything is new?
author: Sri M

text: The paths are many and the goal is total fullness and completeness. We are all seeking though we may not be spiritually inclined. If even a few people understand this and start living this way, we can change the world.
author: Sri M

text: Nobody can give us illumination; we have to find it ourselves. Just as one who is hungry has to find food for oneself.
author: Sri M

text: If we are making spiritual progress, don’t judge by how many visions or kinds of lights one sees. What we have to look at is how one behaves. Have I become less selfish? Has my world narrowed down or has it expanded? Do I feel bad for the child next door or is it only for my child?
author: Sri M

text: If you have an old building and you want to put up a new structure there, what do you do first? You demolish all that is old and constructed, all that is artificial, so that the new comes up. From the Yogi’s point of view or from a spiritual aspirant‘s point of view, every day is a tandava , because without breaking the old images we cannot see anything new.
author: Sri M

text: While structures are important for living and other things, constantly being involved in the structures makes the mind also a physical structure. You are no more free, even the thoughts, the expressions, everything is built up into some kind of design, or structure.
author: Sri M

text: We like to think we live in the present. Most of us live in the past because we cling to the images that we have created and others have created for us. So we actually live in the past.
author: Sri M

text: When you sit down in meditation, images and thoughts of all kinds will come. The way to do it is to break everything.
author: Sri M

text: The most powerful enemy for a yogi, if one is on the spiritual path, is Kamadeva. Kamadeva need not necessarily mean sensual, physical pleasures. Kama means desire.
author: Sri M

text: All the dance systems we have in this country can be traced to the Tandava of Shiva also called Nataraja, Lord of dance. Tandava nritya is a dance of destruction, everything is shaken up, but if you really look into it, understand, destruction is the first step to construction.
author: Sri M

text: Yes, it is worth praying for peace and our prayers do influence and bring about peace in the world.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says, if you want to understand that Supreme reality which pervades everywhere, let go, move from your own centre, expand and let everyone be a part of you.
author: Sri M

text: TThe mind is always asking for something, or it is running away from something. These are the two major factors. Either it is attached to something or it is repelled by something. If these two factors are present, then the chattering will never stop. So can we try to be without too much attachment and too much repulsion? Because if these two things are there, there cannot be quietness of mind. Can we be free of this? I think it is possible.
author: Sri M

text: Every little thing is full of joy. The dew drop you find on the grass in the morning, the breeze that blows in quietly bringing in the perfume of the jasmine, the smell of the earth after the first rains. The ice-clad peaks of the distant mountain, the laughter of the child, the song of the peasant. Everything becomes the festival of joy and the root of it is within oneself. It's only when the inner being becomes joyful that the world becomes full of joy.
author: Sri M

text: The best way to control a wayward mind is an occasional fast. The yogi, a practitioner of spiritual exercises, needs to moderate all his activities in order to be able to progress in his endeavour. Mark you, moderation is the key word.
author: Sri M

text: The aim of yoga is Kaivalya, freedom from all bondage. As long as there is bondage, there is no happiness to be found.
author: Sri M

text: The real Shivam is your inner being, your antar atma. First the mind has to be freed so that the mind begins to understand that the happiness that we seek for in this world is within.
author: Sri M

text: Through the practice of Yoga, understanding and intelligence expand and help to go beyond the ordinary mind. The mind ceases to exist as a separate entity as soon as the vrittis (distractions) are wiped out. Only pure consciousness exists.
author: Sri M

text: The best karma is doing good to others.
author: Sri M

text: The Supreme Brahman is free of all conditionings and it is beyond our five senses, so we cannot do sparsha or touch it by our hands and yet it is manifested in all forms.
author: Sri M

text: The Truth cannot be expressed in words. All definitions fall short. Nor can it be reckoned in Time. It's timeless and tender and words corrupt its purity.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest miracle is to purify the mind and take it towards spiritual fulfillment.
author: Sri M

text: The sound of AUM is the link between this world and the other. It is the juncture between the unknown and the known. AUM is the bridge that takes one across.
author: Sri M

text: The ultimate tandava nritya is when Shiva destroys all the structures and you are left with none other than the pure witness and this pure witness is none other than Shiva, “Chidananda roopah, shivoham, shivoham” , ‘I’ am of the nature of Chit - consciousness and bliss, I am Shivam I am Shivam.
author: Sri M

text: You are the consciousness which is the witness of all the drama, watching in amusement as the ego plays its games, dons different masks at different times and ends up identifying itself with the roles it plays. The real you is that ever-blissful, unchanging, blessed consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: The reservoir of all joy, the essence of all bliss, is in your own heart, in the core of your own being.
author: Sri M

text: Remember! There is no technique to reach the ‘Truth’, for you are yourself the ‘Truth’. Techniques are there to still the mind so that it understands the truth that the mind cannot reach the ‘Self ’ and settles perfectly, so that the ‘Self ’ – the ever-blissful ‘Self ’ – alone shines forth.
author: Sri M

text: As you practise meditation daily, you’ll enter subtler spheres of consciousness and bliss. You will see lights and hear heavenly music and witness wonders, but tarry not. These are merely signposts and sometimes temptations. Keep marching ahead quietly until you come face to face with the ‘Presence’, who is within and not far away.
author: Sri M

text: In the beginning, when you meditate, thoughts will come, sometimes in torrents, but don’t worry. Don’t try to throw them out. Watch calmly as you would a mischievous child and they’ll settle down and disappear.
author: Sri M

text: Thoughts are like ripples that disturb the calm surface of the mind and distort the reflections. When they disappear, the surface becomes clean, and the undistorted reflection of the ‘Sacred One’ is glimpsed, however briefly.
author: Sri M

text: When you get up from your daily meditations, thank everything and everybody with utter humility.
author: Sri M

text: A tension-free mind can think more clearly and without confusion. As you continue to meditate, you’ll see that your thought processes begin to get into efficient mode.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t mistake the technique for the goal. Go on meditating deeper and deeper until the mind is stripped bare and you find your own dear ‘Self ’, the radiant, unpolluted, indestructible, pure consciousness, the unalloyed bliss.
author: Sri M

text: Lead a simple, transparent life full of peace and tranquillity. The small inconveniences you may feel are nothing compared to what you gain.
author: Sri M

text: While rituals and ceremonies may be dispensed with if found unnecessary and cumbersome, yamas and niyamas, the rules of conduct have to be studied carefully and adopted as far as possible, because, by practising them, your capacity to meditate is enhanced.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual life is not incompatible with worldly existence. A properly lived life in the world is conducive to meditation. This is especially true, if you are also inclined to practise asanas, pranayam, etc., as laid down in the path of ashtanga yoga. The Gita puts it in a nutshell by saying, “This yoga is not for one who eats too much, or too little, sleeps too much, or too little.” Moderation is the key word for the hatha yogi and the rajayogi. And this is best provided in a householder’s life.
author: Sri M

text: As far as intoxicants are concerned, one doesn’t have to be extraordinarily intelligent to understand why one is advised to abstain from them. Anything that makes one unbalanced and lose one’s sense of proportion and judgement has to be abandoned.
author: Sri M

text: Sing and dance to your heart’s content. Absorb yourself in devotional music and let it carry you to higher states of consciousness. Once you taste the wine of devotion, you’ll never want to touch lesser intoxicants. But let me caution you. Music must be pure. Full of devotion.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t forget that the aim is union with the Divine, or as some others might put it, ‘sieving the ore to discover pure gold’.
author: Sri M

text: No one can meditate or remain engaged in devotional activities for 24 hours a day. There may be exceptions but we are talking of the general run of mankind. Therefore, find some time when you are engaged neither in earning your bread nor in praying, to do whatever you can for your fellow human beings.
author: Sri M

text: Serve others but remember while doing so to be thankful to them for providing you with the opportunity to serve them and thereby speeding up your spiritual progress. It is you who should be thankful, not they.
author: Sri M

text: Feed one hungry man even once and see how much easier it is to contact the Divinity when you sit down for meditation that day.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation and practice of moral precepts complement each other. Begin to meditate today. Do not postpone it. Side by side with this, attempt to follow the yamas and niyamas to the best of your ability.
author: Sri M

text: As you progress, you’ll become more and more morally perfect and so also will your progress in meditation become better and better. This will go on until you reach your final goal. Till then, there are bound to be imperfections. So don’t worry.
author: Sri M

text: Only when one has perfectly understood that all that exists is the ‘Self ’, will selfishness be completely destroyed. Doesn’t all immorality spring from selfishness? As you approach nearer and nearer the blissful Self, you will find no need to behave immorally. Until then, do your best. Conquer hate with love.
author: Sri M

text: The one sure sign of a true bhakta is the absence of selfishness. If anyone pretends to be one and you discover even a tinge of selfishness, keep away.
author: Sri M

text: When the time is ripe, the master comes. You don’t have to search for him in the Himalayas. He may be living next door but you may not know. Your ignorance and arrogance effectively help him to remain hidden.
author: Sri M

text: If you are a sincere aspirant, if your only goal in life is to meet your beloved ‘Self ’, if you constantly meditate and pray for guidance, the master shall surely come – if so required.
author: Sri M

text: You may or may not recognise him but he guides you silently. The true master is the Lord Himself who takes on various forms to guide the devotee.
author: Sri M

text: Test the master well before you accept him. If there is even a trace of lust or selfishness in him, he is not of the highest status. Test him thoroughly but have patience. Do not judge in haste, for, many a time the actions of a master have been misunderstood. Mysterious are his ways. Do not judge his actions without finding out the motives.
author: Sri M

text: A guide is necessary in almost all cases because you are starting on a voyage of largely unchartered territory.
author: Sri M

text: Do not imitate your own teacher, for you are not he. Follow his teachings and instructions instead, and you’ll bloom into a master in your own original way and not turn out to be a faint imitation, a mere shadow of the original.
author: Sri M

text: A master may be young, old, male, female, fair or dark. The externals do not matter at all. What matters is his inner spiritual status. He may, if he so decides, help you wipe your heart clear of all the accumulated vasanas and make you free. May such a master guide you!
author: Sri M

text: You cannot go looking for a Guru with a magnifying glass; you may not find one anywhere. If you find that someone is not trying to take over your mind, but instead allowing you the freedom to figure out how to handle your mind, then perhaps that is your teacher. Is he interested in helping you or taking help from you?
author: Sri M

text: In the Nath Parampara - the first Guru, teacher is supposed to be Adinath and Adinath is none other than Shiva. Shiva and Adinath are indistinguishable. The most important sadhana is to worship the Guru, look at Him, meditate upon Him, and follow the teachings that He has given; the most important of which is to consider all living beings as part of yourself, because, if you don’t have that, then all this worshipping is no use.
author: Sri M

text: All human beings are constantly searching for something, name, fame, position, wealth, everything. And this search goes on and on till we die. My Guru Maheshwarnath Babaji, used to tell me that RIP is not necessarily ‘rest in peace’. He said it could be ‘Rise if Possible.’
author: Sri M

text: At least in spiritual matters, please don’t lie! Don’t say I meditated for six hours today and the lights were going up and down. Say only what you really feel. If you don’t follow this, it is the greatest blunder that can happen.
author: Sri M

text: To be alert is not to strain but to relax and let the teachings sink deep so that you’ll have no more doubts.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t be afraid of being left alone. When left alone, that's the time you can look into yourself and find out where your problems are. So, appreciate it when you are alone and be thankful to those who have let you be alone.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t be obsessed with what you eat and what you don’t – a trait which Swami Vivekananda called ‘the religion of the kitchen’. Eat what is nutritious, what your body needs. Take medical advice if necessary but eat in moderation.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana cannot cause tiredness, when you are connected with your inner energy. If you are getting exhausted, you need to look at your whole day and see what activity you are engaged in - what have you been eating or what kind of society you are mixing with. When that clashes with your meditative state, it can cause tiredness. So avoid it, and then you'll see you are full of energy, even when you practice sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: If you can cut that fellow called the ego, you can also conquer death. It is this ego which is the cause of all mischief. Try to look at the problem and see how one can purify one's mind and find the essence of reality in one's own heart.
author: Sri M

text: When you do pooja, also do pooja to the deity that is sitting inside and think that, that all--auspicious Ananda, which is called Shivam, is the true essence of your being and if you turn within you can find the completeness, the poornata that we seek. You and your God are one, connected within yourself.
author: Sri M

text: The treasure that you seek is within you, and you seek it outside. It is because we know that a treasure exists that we are seeking. It is built in our system.
author: Sri M

text: Within us, in the depths of our consciousness, there is an element which is the same Purna from which this world has come.
author: Sri M

text: Purna from which the whole world has come and which we seek, is right inside us in our true essence. It is that which the Upanishad calls the Supreme Reality, living in the depths of our consciousness, which the Nirvana Shataka has described as chidananda rupam shivoham shivoham - deep down in the essence of my heart, I am the auspicious Shivam, not this body which lives and which dies.
author: Sri M

text: Live intelligently and wisely, not giving to excesses, purifying your mind, doing your work honestly and at the same time trying to turn inwards and look within, knowing well that the satisfaction that I seek cannot be found anywhere except inside.
author: Sri M

text: It is okay to worship the divine with a form but to ultimately feel it, you need to involve your heart.
author: Sri M

text: The core of our being is the heart, not the heart that pumps blood but when the mind is quiet and everything is clear and clean without any bad thoughts about others, in that settled state we can feel the presence of the divine. Now that treasure is what we should look for.
author: Sri M

text: There are dimensions of the mind which operate beyond our ordinary logical, rational thinking. If we can voluntarily extricate ourselves from our day to day thinking, sometimes perhaps from the conditioned thoughts in our mind, and then open our mind to receiving what is beyond the three dimensional world, perhaps we can tap the infinite potential that is inside our own mind, waiting to be explored.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says, if you want to understand that Supreme reality which pervades everywhere, let go, move from your own centre, expand and let everyone be a part of you.
author: Sri M

text: Every little thing is full of joy. The dew drop you find on the grass in the morning, the breeze that blows in quietly bringing in the perfume of the jasmine, the smell of the earth after the first rains. The ice-clad peaks of the distant mountain, the laughter of the child, the song of the peasant. Everything becomes the festival of joy and the root of it is within oneself. It's only when the inner being becomes joyful that the world becomes full of joy.
author: Sri M

text: The whole purpose of Sadhana, is how to zero in, how to go into the essence of this being, which is not anywhere outside, but within us.
author: Sri M

text: As long as there is a division between the seer and the seen, there is duality. The real seer, after having understood the Brahman, has nothing to see, because the seer itself is what is in the seen.
author: Sri M

text: One of the greatest qualities of human beings is the quality of love because there is no logic to it. For love people do things which are unimaginable. It is a feeling, a compulsive feeling. It is because of this feeling that the whole world evolves. And this love in its highest state is called Devotion.
author: Sri M

text: Thoughts are like ripples that disturb the calm surface of the mind and distort the reflections. When they disappear, the surface becomes clean, and the undistorted reflection of the 'Sacred One' is glimpsed, however briefly.
author: Sri M

text: A retreat is meant for implementation. By implementation I mean the practice of sadhana and the other is the practice of certain principles that are conducive to the practice of sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: The mind has various levels of impurities and agitations. As long as these last, they are like curtains, which very subtly veil or cover the Truth. You are not searching for something outside yourself. To find what you are searching for within, one needs to penetrate so many layers of impurities, which are gathered, not only in this life, but for many hundreds of lives.
author: Sri M

text: The ultimate aim of spiritual fulfillment is to find the Truth - Satya. To reach the Truth, you have to start with being truthful, practically, in day-to-day life. You cannot imagine that you are finding the Truth and remain untruthful all your life.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot expect to find the Universal Truth and speak lies 24 hours a day. Then you are under an illusion. You may think that you have found the Truth, but it may not be the Truth. Because, if you cannot implement it in your day-to-day existence, how can you find the Universal Truth?
author: Sri M

text: When a person enters into the spiritual journey, through practice, he will be faced with greater temptations than the ordinary person.
author: Sri M

text: It is very important that if you have been given a sadhana, practice it with complete attention, without missing a single day and minute of the time which you have been given. Otherwise, it just will not work.
author: Sri M

text: One of the greatest obstacles to meditation is sleep. And without overcoming the desire to sleep, nobody can attain the high goal of turiya . It is not possible. If you are a sadhaka, you have to fight it. There is no other way. Fight it till sleep becomes your slave. Not the other way.
author: Sri M

text: One of the great obstacles, impurities to Truth is sloth. Swami Vivekananda realized it, and implemented it. He said, ‘you fellows cannot meditate 24 hours a day, therefore work’. It prevents you from sleep and sloth. And working for others purifies your heart.
author: Sri M

text: How can I practice kindness? Kindness has to come naturally. Imitating a practitioner of kindness is always better than a fellow who is cruel. Practice kindness to all living beings, as much as possible.
author: Sri M

text: The first characteristic of a person who has attained the spiritual Truth is - the heart and mind become calm, quiet and content.
author: Sri M

text: On the spiritual path, an important requirement is fearlessness. We must not be afraid of public opinion. The last vice that a human being has to overcome is shame.
author: Sri M

text: You have to practice your sadhana. Make time for it and practice as much as possible.
author: Sri M

text: Bring about a change in your day-to-day life and transparency in your character and conduct. Without which we may continue to meditate for years, but nowhere will we go. Because, the first reflection of spiritual perfection is in your day-to-day life. How you deal with it, how you behave, what you do, this is most important.
author: Sri M

text: When we attain the goal, when you touch That, all the effort put into it is worth it. There is nothing more to be attained, there is nothing more valuable. What is more valuable than finding out that you are the Truth and are truly free! Nothing can hold you, nothing can burn you. At the end of it, it is a great achievement.
author: Sri M

text: Atmano mokshartha Jagat hitaya cha. It’s not just the liberation of oneself that one needs to take care of. We should also keep the welfare of the world in mind. A yogi can lead a balanced life only when both these factors are integrated.
author: Sri M

text: Listen to the pure music of the flute. Hopefully, you might go beyond the language to Is-ness. It is the sound of the flute that takes you to Krishna.
author: Sri M

text: Divinity exists in the core of our being, within our hearts. Spiritual life is the way of discovering that divine spark. In the process, one is supposed to do good deeds, through which the world gets better and one learns to live without hurting others. That’s the aim, to discover your true self - who you actually are, in contrast to who one thinks one is.
author: Sri M

text: It’s not necessary to have a Guru, in the case of some people. But I think a guide is required. The Guru should not become more important than the teaching. Then it becomes more of a Guru worship.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is done to purify the mind, free of distractions and to lead a simple life where you can at any time tune in to your inner self, which is divine.
author: Sri M

text: We can get rid of the negatives by substituting them with positives. And understanding comes out of humility. It is the ego that swells up and says, I can do anything, I am the most powerful.
author: Sri M

text: Sankhya is one of the most ancient philosophies which gives you a working knowledge of the world, material world and about Purusha and Prakruti . Prakruti is the world and Purusha is the consciousness. And the aim of Kaivalya is to free oneself from Prakruti and remain in the pure state of Purusha . It considers Prakruti not as an illusion but as an impermanent thing that keeps moving while the Purusha is always there, permanently.
author: Sri M

text: We are afraid that the world we live in and love to hold it together will run away from us. The moment we begin to hold on, the joy is over because you are fighting against it running away. What happiness is there when you are clinging to something! Happiness is there when you are not clinging to anything at all, when you are free and clear.
author: Sri M

text: To free yourself from illusions the senses build for us and how we get caught by it, one of the ways is to be eternally watchful and that watchfulness is called awareness. Buddhists call it mindfulness. Every action you do, just reflect and see, am I doing it for the good of someone or am I actually doing it because I want to satiate my desires.
author: Sri M

text: It’s very difficult to define the ultimate Truth. But in my opinion, it is to discover the divinity within you.
author: Sri M

text: Letting go means not being stuck to the dream world that we have created for ourselves, and to be able to let go of it at any instant. It’s not easy. It's a long journey. We go through many obstacles and difficulties.
author: Sri M

text: Gita is not something to be read as a theoretical text. While you need to do that, it basically should be looked at as a sadhana, a practice by which you free yourself.
author: Sri M

text: In India, we start all our activities by invoking Lord Ganesha, who has a form, shape, and a symbol, but in spite of all the symbols, the scriptures refer to Ganesha in the Ganesha Stavam as : Ajam nirvikalpam niraakaaramekam Niraanandam aanandam advaita poornam Param nirgunam nirvishesham nireeham Para brahma roopam Ganesham bhajema. So when you bow down to Ganesha, think that you are bowing down to the manifestation of that Para Brahman, the Supreme.
author: Sri M

text: We human beings have one unique capacity of being aware that we have consciousness through thought or meditation, but first, the mind has to be stilled. When the mind is still, then something else takes over, which you cannot call actually brain thought. We call it intuition, a presence, or essence.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot think of the soul without consciousness. But consciousness can think without the soul. Because there can be consciousness without even an entity called the soul.
author: Sri M

text: In one hand of Ganesha, you will find a pasha, noose, and the other holds an ankusha, means a goad, used to poke, to make people do the work. In the elephant’s case, it is used to poke the finger so that it moves. Pasha in one hand and ankusha in the other, Modakam in one hand, and one hand in blessing, all these are profound symbols.
author: Sri M

text: Consciousness, according to the Upanishads and according to what we know, is that which can neither be heard nor smelled, not tasted, not seen. So none of these things are going to be of any help. But without that, none of these things can work.
author: Sri M

text: The pasha in Ganesha’s hand is the noose with which divinity, if it lays its eyes on someone and wants that person to be attracted to itself. Without that noose no one can be pulled towards Divinity.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot catch consciousness. It's necessary to meditate to bring the mind to that state where it can at least recognize that there is something beyond it. That can happen only when the mind can be brought to tranquil, peaceful, quiet wavelengths. So therefore, all the practices of yoga of all kinds are meant to bring this about.
author: Sri M

text: The modakam is which the mooshak is eyeing all the time. Modakam is sweet and also means full satisfaction. It is the fruit of wisdom of the understanding of the Brahman; eat it and you are caught and then you will be taken upwards if you are ready.
author: Sri M

text: Ganesha is a symbol of that real aspirant, sincere aspirant who knows that there is no point in going all over the world searching for happiness, you need to just go around the Shivam, Chidananda Roopam Shivoham Shivoham, who sits inside our heart.
author: Sri M

text: Vigneshwara is the one who removes all obstacles from you.
author: Sri M

text: Ganesha represents the actual beginning of transcendence of consciousness from the gross to subtle.
author: Sri M

text: If I see inside me a light, it cannot be that I'm peculiar, that only I have the light. The light is in everybody's heart. It may be covered or hiding, but the spark is there.
author: Sri M

text: Jesus said, the foxes have dens and the snakes have holes. The son of man knows not where to lay his head. In the Bhagavad Gita, such a yogi is called aniketa, one who has no home.
author: Sri M

text: Joy is something that is inside you. You need to just go in and look at yourself in your pure state, which means when your mind is tranquil, calm, when there is no disturbance in your mind, there's no opposing battles going on inside, there's a joy that wells up in you, which is so beautiful. And you don't have to buy it anywhere. It's your own.
author: Sri M

text: There's only one mind and it is working through different centers. So if there is one mind, if I feel the pain of others, the compassion from me will pass on to that person, and the whole thing begins to get a new life.
author: Sri M

text: ‘If you are the all-knowing supreme being, you know what I need. Please grant me what I need.’ This is the humblest prayer that one can make. Very often what we need in our evolution is perhaps not what we want. One needs to make a little distinction.
author: Sri M

text: Breath is the most important thing in our lives. You can do without a drink, you can do without food, but one minute without breath is impossible. So watch your breath and pay attention to it.
author: Sri M

text: Shunya means no thing. It's not nothing, but it's not a thing that I can define or you can define. It cannot be that "Shunya" is nothing because this whole world is supposed to have come out of it.
author: Sri M

text: The brain has to have space. You need to keep it clear. If you don't have an empty vessel, how will you receive? The vessel must be totally shunya, then what is received is purna.
author: Sri M

text: If you really are calm and composed, nothing will ruffle you. Then you also develop fearlessness. And if you are fearless, then you can achieve and move forward to things which the person who begins to be afraid cannot move forward.
author: Sri M

text: Thought is limited. Good things and mischief all are included in thought. When I say, now I am free of all thought, who is saying that thought? Even that is a thought. So, it's only when one understands this and everything cools down, then there is something that the brain cannot touch. That can touch the brain.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes great teachers say, dump all this intellectual stuff, go directly. What they mean is open the heart instead of the brain. And when they say heart, they are talking about the ultimate, not the physical heart which is beating inside.
author: Sri M

text: Liberation is a very difficult word to understand because it has many meanings. To be liberated from the ordinary mode of thinking is the first step in liberation.
author: Sri M

text: The final liberation, which we call moksha, is to realize that there is nothing to be liberated. Everything is free. Already.
author: Sri M

text: If the truth is all pervasive, then the good, bad, ugly, all are part of it. There is nothing here or there or anywhere, which does not consist of the principle of the Supreme reality.
author: Sri M

text: Divinity is that which sustains us, although we think we are sustaining ourselves.
author: Sri M

text: Creation starts with Shakti. According to the Agamas, when everything is at rest, there is only Shivam. When there is kinetic movement, it becomes Shakti. Shiva without the Shakti becomes Shava.
author: Sri M

text: Prayer is something that comes from the heart of the human being. We are all in some way limited. But at least we have a hypothesis that the Supreme God or reality is not like us. It is unlimited. Except the Vedantin of course who says it is the same. So then what do we do when we are helpless? We pray.
author: Sri M

text: If a person has totally surrendered, he is free of all misery immediately.
author: Sri M

text: Through praying for others, you purify your mind, until nothing remains for you to pray except to be one with the infinite.
author: Sri M

text: For moksha there is no shortcut. You have to go through many things in life before you get there. If anybody says there is a shortcut to moksha, then you are being fooled, run away.
author: Sri M

text: There are simple prayers in all religions. Most of them say, give me this day my daily bread. Normally there is no harm in that. But please add this also, ‘in the ultimate essence, please lead me to you.’ Keep this in mind, Why am I here? What am I doing in these little things? Is there something beyond?
author: Sri M

text: In Sankhya, it is discussed that there are three gunas which govern our nature - sattva guna, rajo guna, tamo guna. Everybody has these gunas but ratios are different.
author: Sri M

text: Shivam cannot be touched without the activation of the Shakti. Without the havan kund, no homa can be done.
author: Sri M

text: Letting go means not to carry the hurts and feelings from yesterday to today. This is the greatest letting go. Which means not to form an image of somebody and keep it always in our head so that we don't see the person as the person changes.
author: Sri M

text: The Energy and the Power that is manifested all over the world, right from the energy that you see in a tiny amoeba that moves, gets its food and eats it – all is Power. Now, power generates power – so the amoeba eats and gets more energy. This energy is a constantly renewing force, which is also called Para Shakti. It is the highest power.
author: Sri M

text: Nobody has only good qualities. There are special individuals sometimes who come into this world, who have hardly any bad qualities. Even such people, to remain in this world, develop a little bit of tamo guna and get some quality, otherwise they will fly off.
author: Sri M

text: Good-bad is a very relative thing that we have worked out in society. Nobody is totally bad. Everybody has an element of goodness in them. What is good for me may be bad for somebody else. The less selfish one is, the better one is.
author: Sri M

text: If you start from the time you are born till the time you are in the present, you have already passed through many things similar to past lives. Very similar - what all roles we have played. From childhood one role, then when you grow up another role, when you are an adult another role. We think we are the same but we keep changing.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is only a collection of conditioned thoughts. The brain is conditioned by the circumstances in which you are born and how you are trained, and the five senses operate. So, it is quite normal and natural. But when the mind learns to pull in the senses inside, and enjoys what is inside, then slowly it gets free.
author: Sri M

text: If the God to whom you are praying is omniscient, who knows everything, then do you have to tell him that this is what I want? Therefore I pray that you know best what is necessary. Please give me what is right for me.
author: Sri M

text: If somebody calls someone a fool, it is a wonderful thing. You are happy because you are a fool and nobody will ask you anything.That is fine. But because of that, one should not give up kindness. In the long run, kindness is a wonderful thing. It keeps my mind happy and in peace.
author: Sri M

text: Ordinary thought is our logical thought. It is linear. But what if the truth that we seek, if we are seeking, is everywhere, isha vasya, idam sarvam, there is no place where it is not there. In that case, how can you approach it in a linear way? When all approaching and movement stops, then what remains is the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: When the Kundalini merges with the Paramatman, which is the blissful being at the crown center, the Yogi is absorbed in an ecstasy, which far exceeds the ecstasy which any ordinary human being has ever experienced before.
author: Sri M

text: As the yogi progresses in kundalini sadhana, the body becomes light, mind becomes light, there is a glow, internal glow, and also sometimes an external glow on the face. The voice becomes peaceful and pleasing to hear and usually the yogi is free of serious diseases.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual life cannot be diverse from day to day life. The inner attitude is more important.
author: Sri M

text: The common factors across human beings are: same desires, same jealousies, same problems, same dissatisfactions, same rancor inside! Can I accept that? Can I treat, in my mind, everyone the same? After all, all the human beings are the same!
author: Sri M

text: The theory of Karma presupposes the existence of this body, apart from this life, somewhere in the past. Our present is a reflection of our past. What I had done before decides what I am today.
author: Sri M

text: As we have no idea as to when we will be ultimately free, the only work we can do is, now, so that we can be free from all conditioning in the future. When we go deeper and deeper into the core of our consciousness, we can break the fretters one by one to a large extent.
author: Sri M

text: To lead a family life is a good way to test yourself. Only your spouse knows who you are. Outside we can put up many poses. They see you from close quarters so they know how you behave! It’s a very nice meter to check yourself, to check your ego also as to how it functions. Consider that as training. If you think your spiritual enquiry is very important, it is possible to do it under all circumstances. Those circumstances should be taken as tests.
author: Sri M

text: Most of our anger is not because of hunger or physical discomfort but it is because of mental discomfort. Non-fulfillment of desires, regret that we have done something which we should not have, regret that we have ourselves worked into a situation from which we cannot come out now. There are so many – you have to look at it carefully.
author: Sri M

text: By silence does not mean the absence of sound, which can be easily achieved. Deaf people are in silence. Silence means the complete stopping of the chattering of the mind.
author: Sri M

text: Remember! There is no technique to reach the Truth, for you are yourself the Truth. Techniques are there to still the mind so that it understands the truth that the mind cannot reach the Self and settles perfectly, so that the ever-blissful Self - alone shines forth.
author: Sri M

text: Step firmly upon the path. Have no fear. Fearlessness is close to 'Truth'.
author: Sri M

text: Visualize your desires in complete detail and you are sure to attain them, but never visualise harm to others, for that will arrest your own spiritual development and pull you down the ladder of spiritual evolution.
author: Sri M

text: Nama Japa is the easiest way to keep continuous remembrance of the Divine in today's world. Some prefer the abstract way of engaging the mind in nothingness, but that is not easy to do.
author: Sri M

text: You are the consciousness which is the witness of all the drama, watching in amusement as the ego plays its games, dons different masks at different times and ends up identifying itself with the roles it plays. The real you is that ever-blissful, unchanging, blessed consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: Consciousness also means Sakshi, the witness. The all pervading consciousness is also the witness to all that happens. It appears to participate but does not participate. Find that witness in yourself. Now, not tomorrow. Today. Right now.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishads are not a doctrine but are in the form of open discussion between teacher and disciple. The teacher does not pretend to know everything. When young men would go to a Rishi, he would say, "stay with me for three months and I shall teach you, if I know? That is the depth of Upanishads.
author: Sri M

text: When the artificial barrier disappears, all that remains is the field in which so many thoughts appear and disappear. As I watch the appearing and disappearing of thoughts perfectly aware that I, the watcher, am only a part of that unceasing wave of thoughts, my mind begins to rest.
author: Sri M

text: Of course, the master tests your patience. Therefore, knock persistently but wait patiently. Then your heart will be filled with supreme bliss and you will work for the good of mankind.
author: Sri M

text: If we can stay with sorrow – sometimes something may happen. We may blow up with intense sorrow but that blowing up is very good blowing up. Why don’t we blow up all the artificial barriers that we have created? It’s of no use anyway.
author: Sri M

text: The advantage of meditating early in the morning is that you have not yet started your day, so, the distractions of the day do not exist. Second, that is the only time you are not caught up in anything. You have just had a good rest and have woken up so your mind is still fresh and quiet to some extent.
author: Sri M

text: Thinking itself is ‘mind’. When there are thoughts, automatically there is the mind. Therefore, it implies that where there is no thought there is no mind, from the ordinary sense of the term.
author: Sri M

text: This human body and this human world into which we come are full of sorrow from all sides. Since it is the only vehicle which leads us to moksha, it is very precious.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual path nearly always, except in cases of certain gifted individuals who have been born with spiritual faculties, requires a guide; because we are largely walking on unexplored territory. It’s not a usually walked path. It is an unexplored territory.
author: Sri M

text: In ancient India, the young aspirant, brahmachari went to the masters, the Rishis , seeking not wealth, health, or position, but pure and unconditioned freedom. And this pure, unconditioned, unbound freedom is called moksha or mukti .
author: Sri M

text: According to Vedanta that feeling of being dependent on what is around you, the feeling that you are bound and that you have to get out of it, is part of the great illusion of the mind called the Maya .
author: Sri M

text: When one has reached the Sun, the spiritual Sun that is eternal and fearless, one does not have to come back into this world of sorrow. That is the final goal.
author: Sri M

text: When one has reached the Sun, the spiritual Sun that is eternal and fearless, one does not have to come back into this world of sorrow. That is the final goal.
author: Sri M

text: All things about spiritual matters boil down to your day to day relationships. We can sit at home and meditate for hours but when we come out and (we have not changed for the better) are still the same, it does not work.
author: Sri M

text: Following the teachings is more important than worshipping the Teacher.
author: Sri M

text: The most important function of the Guru is to act as a well-polished mirror so that we see ourselves as we are, with all our imperfections. The teacher reflects what is going on in us. Sometimes this can be very unpleasant. A genuine spiritual teacher is not worried about the unpleasantness. When it gets very unpleasant, many people leave. What a teacher is looking for is not numbers but to see if one person can change. If we can change one person, that’s enough to change the world.
author: Sri M

text: The key principle of the teaching is that we are in our true essence complete and full. It’s because we haven’t recognised this that we are looking for it outside.
author: Sri M

text: You are the consciousness which is the witness of all the drama, watching in amusement as the ego plays its games, dons different masks at different times and ends up identifying itself with the roles it plays. The real you is that ever-blissful, unchanging, blessed consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: Sorrows and shortcomings, the cares of this world, are certainly there, but who doesn’t have them? Now you, the traveler on the path, should know that they are lessons for you, and that after each obstacle is overcome, the road becomes smoother and easier.
author: Sri M

text: If someone promises salvation for all at once, take care; you are about to be hoodwinked. If someone guarantees to lead you to Supreme Bliss in a certain number of days, again, be on guard. No human being can ensure it; only God can.
author: Sri M

text: The ‘Self ’ is ever free, ever blissful. It is and was never bound; therefore, there is no question of making it free. It is always free. It manifests itself as the ‘I’, the consciousness, the ‘I’ that exists eternally in the waking state, dream state, and deep sleep, the ‘witness’ of all states of consciousness. This is the real ‘you’, the blessed, blissful ‘Self ’. The mind, borrowing the ‘I’ from it, mistakenly feels bound and attempts to make itself free.
author: Sri M

text: There is no technique to reach the ‘Truth’, for you are yourself the ‘Truth’. There are techniques to still the mind so that it understands the truth that the mind cannot reach the ‘Self ’ and settles perfectly, so that the ‘Self ’ – the ever-blissful ‘Self ’ – alone shines forth.
author: Sri M

text: Thoughts are like ripples that disturb the calm surface of the mind and distort the reflections. When they disappear, the surface becomes clean, and the undistorted reflection of the ‘Sacred One’ is glimpsed, however briefly.
author: Sri M

text: When you get up from your daily meditations, thank everything and everybody with utter humility.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation is a word used in English which means many things to many people. If you go back to the Indian sources, the word meditation is actually split into three. There is dharana, there is dhyana and there is samadhi. All these three things put together is what we call ‘meditation’ in English.
author: Sri M

text: Dharana means to be able to fix your attention on something exclusively without being distracted or disturbed by anything else. This comes through training and only through training, because our mind is usually in the habit of being distracted all the time.
author: Sri M

text: Dhyana comes from the root dhi , which means ‘to meditate’. When dharana becomes continuous, like when you pour oil from a vessel, then that dhara , dharana, becomes dhyana. If you are seriously interested in a subject, then dhyana is automatic. If you are not, then through the practice of dharana, it stretches and becomes dhyana.within us.
author: Sri M
